items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: Then you listen to the trombone and you’ve got J.J. Johnson. ... And I’ve learned things from all those musicians.

ctx.x: Probably someone has asked you in the past about your grounding, of those artists. Who do you feel you sort of came out of?

Well I like to say I steal from everybody. I mean well the original obviously would be Charlie Parker, because someone said, that’s where you start. My father was giving me Gene Ammons and Sonny Stitt records so I was listening to that, then came Charlie Parker, then someone said well you need to listen to Dexter Gordon, then I went to see him, then somebody said well okay now you’ve got to check out a guy named Sonny Rollins. Okay you’ve got Sonny Rollins, okay, what about Lucky Thompson. Okay, what about…

flattering, but it got to a point, it didn’t hurt my feelings but at a certain point where I said wow, there’s other things in there than just Joe Henderson. But for whatever reason, people heard that and you still, again, you just keep building and try to go through the wall. And after a while you let some other influences come into my life and the fact of the matter was there was a lot of Joe Henderson paid attention to by me. And so once I started letting some other things seep through, some other styles, some…
